name: Varroc Engineering Ltd
title: Varroc Engineering Ltd - 541578 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue up 12.8% with India EBITDA up 14% and overseas up 24%, but group PBT margin only 4.5% and net debt rose to INR 495 crore; FY27 capex guided INR 450-500 crore, next year INR 300-400 crore.

capex.quote: The CapEx, I think overall will be at least to the tune of between INR 450-500 crores, is what we see as the overall CapEx for this year.

triggers.quote: The overseas order book for this year was around close to INR 1,400 crore.

triggers.label: Net working capital stress; net debt up INR 115 crore
triggers.quote: Also some temporary challenges in net working capital, which should get corrected in the coming quarters.

triggers.label: Debt held at INR 500-600 crore; zero debt targeted FY28
triggers.quote: The average debt could be in the range of INR 500 crore-INR 600 crore, more or less at the current levels or slightly upwards.

triggers.label: Tier 2/3 supplier shortages; normalising after 15 May
triggers.quote: It's mainly to do with bought-out components, not so much with the raw material.

In FY 2027, margins will be higher than what we reported in FY 2026.

guidance.value: Romania EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; Italy forging ~1 year
guidance.quote: Only in Romania we have significant challenge, and we should reach EBITDA breakeven by Q4.

red_flags.quote: somehow, we've not been able to participate in the industry growth which we have seen

red_flags.quote: Tier 2, Tier 3, is where we are facing challenges.

red_flags.quote: there's still a point in our auditor's report with regards to that.

evasions.topic: Growth vs industry and largest customer
evasions.quote: That is essentially why I would say through Q4, we are a little bit behind.
We don't want to give any specific timeframe to it.

summary.headline: Varroc Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.8% YoY to INR 23.7bn, with EBITDA margin at 9.7% and record order intake of INR 33bn.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 23,681 million, with EBITDA margin of 9.7% (vs 9.3% in Q3) and PBT before JV profit of 4.5% (vs 4.4%). FY26 revenue reached INR 88.9bn (+9%), EBITDA margin 9.4% and PBT margin 4.3%, with India PBT margin at 7.2%. Management cited record FY26 order intake of about INR 33bn, roughly 65% EV-linked, and said overseas revenue grew 24% in Q4, with a turnaround expected from 2H FY27. Net debt fell about INR 253 crore YoY to about INR 495 crore after a rise from the September low of INR 318 crore, driven by the VRS scheme and working capital.

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Q4 top line grew about 1-12% YoY (figures differ between speakers), EBITDA +14% and PBT +27%. FY26 India EBITDA 11.7%, PBT 7.2%; management says India PBT is already 8%+ in Q4.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 24% YoY in Q4. Two-wheeler overseas business is slightly EBITDA positive; Romania electronics targets EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; Italian forging may take about one more year. Overseas share of revenue is about 7%, targeted near 10% by end FY27.

segments.name: R&D
segments.commentary: R&D spend was about INR 34 crore at EBITDA level in Q4. The R&D business is not expected to break even within the two-year overseas breakeven horizon.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth: management said mid-to-high teens growth is achievable (Investec question answered 'Yes'); Chairman said INR 9,000 crore-plus revenue will be achieved.
FY27 margins expected to be higher than FY26 (Investec-raised question; answer attributed to IR head).
Overseas order book of about INR 1,400 crore; most programs start production in FY27, with the full contribution in FY28.

Overseas breakeven: two-wheeler already slightly positive, Romania EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, Italian forging about one more year; overall overseas operations (ex-R&D) targeted to break even in about two years.
Debt: no reduction expected in FY27 with average net debt INR 500-600 crore; zero-debt objective by FY28.
Long-term PBT ambition of 10%, with no specific timeframe; management declined to guide on an EBITDA double-digit date.
Capex FY27 about INR 450-500 crore including land; FY28 possibly INR 300-400 crore.
Dividend of 150% of face value recommended; net debt to equity 0.27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of at least INR 450-500 crore, including some land purchase; land availability is constrained and other options are being explored.
Next year (FY28) capex could be lower at about INR 300-400 crore, mainly for capacity and program-related growth capex.
Capex focus: EV and electronics, lighting, and mechanisation/automation on India shop floors to reduce manpower dependence.
Supplier-side capacity expansion is being pursued alongside internal expansion to support higher sales levels.
Thailand lighting plant to start in a small way from December (per CFO).
demand_pricing: Industry growth Q4 YoY: two-wheelers +20.7%, three-wheelers +32.4%, passenger vehicles +11.3%, commercial vehicles +19.5%; FY26 two-wheelers +11.8%, three-wheelers +23.9%.
Varroc underperformed industry in Q4 because growth came from lower-content customer/model mix; management said production data is tracking on track.
Pricing: inflation across commodities expected to be passed through to OEMs with a lag of at least a quarter, with full compensation expected; no material Q4 margin impact.
Supply-side: Tier 2/3 supplier shortages (bought-out components, labour linked to the Middle East conflict) eased after 15 May, with supplier normalisation expected by end of May.
Bajaj Auto share of revenue has declined with execution of a non-Bajaj-skewed order book; share was flat from nine months to full year per IR head.
Non-Bajaj share of revenue reportedly around 44%; non-Bajaj share of EV revenue about 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Split of overseas order book and ramp-up timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas order book about INR 1,400 crore for the year, including Thailand exterior (passenger vehicle) lighting and a headlamp win; most programs start in FY27, with the full potential in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex rise with the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex at least INR 450-500 crore including land, with land options being explored; FY28 possibly INR 300-400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volumes dip QoQ and what is the inflation recovery lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 had backlog recovery; Q4 volumes broadly steady and aftermarket seasonally light. Inflation recovery from OEMs expected with at least a one-quarter lag, with full compensation expected.

qa_highlights.question: Overseas breakeven timing and ATV forging divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Romania EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 and Italian forging about one year more; forging sale being explored alongside internal fixes, with no rush to sell at any price.

qa_highlights.question: Debt trajectory and zero-debt goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt not expected to fall in FY27; average net debt INR 500-600 crore; zero-debt objective by FY28, while pursuing growth capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 growth lag industry and EV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth came from segments with lower content per vehicle, so Varroc lagged in Q4; it expects incremental EV penetration and premiumisation to help.

risks_watch: Revenue growth lagging industry and EV growth in Q4, attributed to customer and model mix.
Net debt rising to INR 495 crore with FY27 debt flat at INR 500-600 crore; zero-debt target by FY28 depends on cash generation.
Commodity inflation and recovery lag with OEMs; Middle East conflict impact on supply chain and labour.
Overseas breakeven timelines (Romania Q4 FY27, Italian forging about one year, R&D later) and possible ATV forging sale.
Net worth fell INR 2,528 million in FY26 due to VRS and other charges; TYC arbitration to conclude by end FY27, per auditor's report point.
Non-auto business wins (motors and motor controls, about INR 50 crore annual peak revenue) are early-stage and expected to scale only next year.
Pending order announcements with top three EV two-wheeler players.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book conversion, EV and overseas turnaround, and FY27 growth, but cautious on near-term debt and vague on margin timing. Management declined to guide on the double-digit EBITDA date and on specific non-auto sizing, and gave some inconsistent figures on Q4 growth.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA for the quarter was around 9.7% as compared to 9.3% in the previous quarter.
We should move to a zero debt status by end of next year.
The order book we are confident in. We don't need to worry.
We're not in a hurry to sell it at any cost.
